target_subject: a human hand inserting a black electrical plug into a wall socket

scene: A white painted brick wall with a mounted white triple electrical outlet panel.
The outlet panel contains three sockets: one round two-pin, one round two-pin with grounding holes, and one rectangular coaxial or data port.
A black insulated power cord extends from the plug being inserted.
action: A right hand grips a black two-pin European-style plug and pushes it into the middle socket.
The plug is partially inserted; metal pins are visible entering the socket apertures.
The hand’s fingers are curled around the plug body, thumb on top, index finger on side.
rationale: The plug appears to be a Type C (Europlug) due to its two round pins and lack of grounding prongs, consistent with the socket shape.
The presence of a coaxial/data port suggests this is a modern multi-function wall plate, common in residential or office settings.
The hand’s orientation and grip suggest intentional insertion rather than accidental contact, though intent cannot be confirmed visually.
object: The wall is made of brick covered with uneven white paint, showing texture and minor imperfections.

The outlet panel is white plastic, rectangular, with three vertically aligned sockets: leftmost is a coaxial/data port with a central pinhole, middle is a round two-pin socket with grounding slots, rightmost is a round two-pin socket without grounding slots.
The plug is black plastic with two parallel round metal pins protruding from its front face.
The cord attached to the plug is black, smooth-surfaced, and exits diagonally downward from the plug’s rear.
The hand has light skin tone, visible knuckles and fingernails, and no jewelry or tattoos.
